title: Desk Guidance — Delinquent Status on Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts
content:
**When an account becomes delinquent.** An active account in the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts becomes delinquent when any quarterly report is still unfiled, or any contribution, bill, penalty or interest still unpaid, the delinquency days after its due date.

**When it returns to active.** A delinquent account is returned to active only when every overdue report is filed and the unpaid balance of the quarter is zero for every overdue quarter. A payment plan or a promise to pay does not cure it. The unpaid balance of a quarter is the contributions or reimbursement billed for the quarter less the payments and credits applied to that component of the quarter, never below zero.

**Effect on the next rate year.** An account still delinquent for a missing report on the computation date moves to the delinquent reporting class for the next rate year under the class placement rule.

## Points of judgement for a return to active

| Every overdue report filed | Unpaid balance zero for every overdue quarter | Payment plan or promise to pay on file | Returned to active |
|---|---|---|---|
| No | Yes | Any | No |
| Yes | No | Any | No |
| No | No | Any | No |
| Yes | Yes | Any | Both conditions of the rule are met |

A payment plan or a promise to pay never stands in for either condition.

## Timing illustration (hypothetical, delinquency days of 30)

A report due on 30 April that is still unfiled on 30 May, the 30th calendar day after its due date, makes an active account delinquent. A report due on 30 April and filed on 29 May does not, on that ground.
